flat.reason: The Codex Guide is record-only by its approved rulebook and carries no story (bible §8 rule 12). A quiet room off the Gate, plainly the Guide's.
The Guide's own page — record-only by the same rulebook. Flat by design.
A blind measurement instrument; a scene beside it would contaminate the blindness it exists to protect. Flat, always.
A held session space; nothing is scattered or staged into a session. Flat.
A life story. No play in it — it stands as a written page, reached with respect from the Gate.
Self-examination; staging it risks exactly the guilt framing the house forbids. A quiet flat room.
The repository's own front door — a document about the work, not a room of the site.
The Sphere's receipt shelf — a documentation page that names the sources behind the instrument's numbers. Record, not story country; flat by design.
The methods page — how the Sphere and the calendar compute, and the evidence labels explained once. Documentation; flat by design.

lands.character: A wooded clearing at the road's beginning, where the Sparks live — and where your own Spark's home stands.
lands.name: The Clearing

nextStep.label: Read the year on the Wheel

lands.character: Thirteen raised beds in a walled garden, one waking per moon, planted from the real farm record.
lands.name: The Garden of Thirteen Beds

nextStep.label: Do a small practice in the Yard

lands.character: A hill crowned with thirteen standing stones — the year seen whole. From the Wheel, look up: the Sphere turns above it.
lands.name: The Wheel

nextStep.label: Plant by the moons in the Garden

lands.character: A crossroads where five roads meet: one desk, one lantern, two books — the tale and the account.
lands.name: The Desk at the Crossroads

nextStep.label: Weigh a word in the Word-Hoard

lands.character: A hoard-room of drawers and labelled shelves, where words are kept like seeds.
lands.name: The Word-Hoard

nextStep.label: Try a system in the Roundhouse

lands.character: Shelved halls that go deep — lamplight, bound pages, and the oldest rooms of the house. The halls are the doorway; the text inside stays a reading room.

lands.character: A high library on the far hill: the pattern under the road, kept on boards and in tall shelves.
lands.name: The High Library

nextStep.label: Weigh a claim on the Proving Grounds

lands.name: The Proving Grounds

nextStep.label: See what is made at the Registry

lands.character: A working roundhouse and workshop yard — nothing believed until it has been tried.
lands.name: The Roundhouse

lands.character: A small round listening room on its own rise — the world's smallest land.
lands.name: The Sound Observatory

nextStep.label: Read deep in the Lore Halls

lands.character: An open yard for small things done daily, by hand — try first, then the reveal.
lands.name: The Practice Yard

nextStep.label: Hear your story so far at the Desk

lands.character: A registry stall and a storehouse: made things entered in the book before they are offered, sealed packages on shelves.
lands.name: The Registry & Storehouse

lands.character: The gate where the road appears — the whole world as a raised relief on the Atlas Room's long table, under today's sky.
lands.name: The World Gate

note: The Codex World's lands, defined over the site catalog (docs/data/site-catalog.json) per the approved world design (Nov 20, 2026). Every catalog entry is accounted for exactly once: shelved in one of the thirteen lands, named as the road (the Caravan), named as the sky (the Sphere), or named flat by design with its reason. scripts/build-world-lands.mjs validates this accounting against the catalog and generates docs/assets/js/world-lands.js — the data the World Gate is drawn from, so the map can never drift from the site. Land order is the design's table order; the moon-to-land count for 'today's land' follows this order (Moon N opens land N).

road.note: The Caravan is not a land. It is the road itself — the travelling way between lands, told in five stages.

sky.note: The Sphere is not a land. It is the sky over the whole world — the calendar's face — reached by looking up. Its works are untouched.
